cur:monumental-san-lorenzo-triumphal-arc.summary: Above the arch of the 6th-century basilica, Christ sits on a blue globe at the centre, holding a cross-staff and raising his hand, flanked by Peter, Lawrence and Pope Pelagius II with a model of his church on one side, and Paul, Stephen and Hippolytus on the other; the jewelled cities of Bethlehem and Jerusalem fill the corners. The mosaic marks Pelagius's rebuilding of the shrine over Saint Lawrence's tomb.
facts: Pope Pelagius II built a church over Saint Lawrence's tomb in the 580s; in the 13th century Honorius III built a new church in front of it, and the old triumphal arch now faces into the later choir.
Pelagius II, who holds the model of the church, died of plague in 590 and was succeeded by Gregory the Great.
